concepts.def: The law of conservation of mass states that no atoms are lost or made during a chemical reaction, so the mass of the products equals the mass of the reactants.

In a chemical reaction the atoms present at the start are the same atoms present at the end; they are only joined together in different ways. Because the atoms are the same atoms, the total mass cannot change.

The reactants are the substances written on the left of an equation and the products are the substances written on the right. Conservation of mass compares the total mass of all the reactants with the total mass of all the products, including any that are gases.

A symbol equation in which there is the same number of atoms of each element on both sides of the equation. Because no atoms are lost or made, every correct symbol equation for a reaction must balance in this way.

Making the numbers of atoms of each element equal on both sides by writing multipliers in normal script in front of formulae. The formulae themselves are never altered, because changing a formula changes the substance the equation describes.
A number written in normal script immediately before a formula. It multiplies every atom in that whole formula: 2Ca(OH)₂ means two of everything the formula contains, that is 2 Ca, 4 O and 4 H atoms.

A small number written below the line inside a formula. It multiplies only the symbol immediately before it: in H₂SO₄ the subscript 2 applies to hydrogen alone and the subscript 4 to oxygen alone, giving 2 H, 1 S and 4 O atoms.
A subscript written after a closing bracket multiplies everything inside the bracket. In Mg(NO₃)₂ the subscript 2 applies to the whole NO₃ group, giving 1 Mg, 2 N and 6 O atoms.
The relative mass of an atom of an element, read from the periodic table. It is a ratio, so it has no units. Relative atomic masses are the values added together to find a relative formula mass.

The relative formula mass (Mr) of a compound is the sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in the numbers shown in the formula. For CaCO₃ this is 40 + 12 + (3 x 16) = 100. Like Ar, it has no units.

concepts.term: Relative formula mass of a molecular element
concepts.def: The same rule is used for an element written as a molecule. For O₂ the relative formula mass is 2 x 16 = 32, because the formula shows two oxygen atoms.

concepts.term: Conservation of relative formula mass in an equation
concepts.def: In a balanced chemical equation, the sum of the relative formula masses of the reactants in the quantities shown equals the sum of the relative formula masses of the products in the quantities shown. The multipliers in front of the formulae must be included in both totals.

concepts.term: Percentage by mass of an element in a compound
concepts.def: The share of a compound's relative formula mass contributed by one element: (Ar of the element x number of its atoms in the formula) divided by the Mr of the compound, then multiplied by 100. In CaCO₃ the oxygen is (3 x 16) / 100 x 100 = 48%.

A change in the reading on a balance during a reaction. Some reactions may appear to involve a change in mass, but this can usually be explained because a reactant or product is a gas and its mass has not been taken into account.

concepts.term: Mass increase when a metal reacts with oxygen
concepts.def: When a metal reacts with oxygen the mass of the oxide produced is greater than the mass of the metal, because oxygen atoms from the air have been added to the solid being weighed.

concepts.term: Thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate
concepts.def: Heating a metal carbonate breaks it down: carbon dioxide is produced and escapes into the atmosphere, leaving the metal oxide as the only solid product. The mass of solid left is therefore less than the mass of carbonate heated.

Apparatus that is open to the air, so gases can enter it or leave it during a reaction. Mass is still conserved overall; it is only the mass sitting on the balance that changes, because some of the substance has moved into or out of the apparatus.
Apparatus sealed so that no particles can enter or leave, such as a stoppered flask. Any gas made stays inside and is still weighed, so the balance reading does not change during the reaction.

concepts.term: Particle model explanation of a mass change
concepts.def: Explaining a balance reading by saying which particles have crossed the boundary of the apparatus. Gas particles are spread far apart and are invisible, but they still have mass, so particles leaving lower the reading and particles joining from the air raise it.

Whenever a measurement is made there is always some uncertainty about the result obtained. Uncertainty is a statement of the interval within which the true value is expected to lie; it is not the same thing as a mistake.

The pattern formed by a set of repeated measurements when they are set out, for example in a table, a scatter of points on a number line or a bar chart. Displaying the distribution shows how closely the repeats agree and makes any odd value obvious.
The sum of a set of repeated measurements divided by how many there are. The mean is the value the uncertainty is quoted about, and it is calculated after any anomalous result has been left out.
A measurement that lies well outside the distribution formed by the others. It is identified and excluded before the mean and the range are worked out, otherwise it would distort both.
The difference between the largest and the smallest value in a set of measurements. For 24.10, 24.15 and 24.20 cm³ the range is 24.20 - 24.10 = 0.10 cm³.

The range of a set of measurements about the mean is used as a measure of uncertainty: the result is quoted as the mean plus or minus half the range. A mean of 24.15 cm³ with a range of 0.10 cm³ is written 24.15 ± 0.05 cm³. A wider range means a larger uncertainty.

mcqs.q: Which statement is the law of conservation of mass?
options: Atoms are destroyed when a gas escapes, so the mass of the products falls.
The masses are equal only when the reaction happens in a sealed container.
The number of molecules is unchanged, so the total mass cannot change.
No atoms are lost or made, so the products have the same mass as the reactants.
mcqs.explain: This is the law as the specification states it: the atoms are conserved, and the equality of masses follows from that.

mcqs.q: 4.8 g of magnesium is heated in air and reacts completely with 3.2 g of oxygen. What is the mass of magnesium oxide formed?
mcqs.explain: All the atoms in both reactants end up in the oxide, so its mass is 4.8 + 3.2 = 8.0 g.

mcqs.q: Which equation for the reaction of sodium with water is correctly balanced?
options: Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂
2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂
2Na + H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂
2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + 2H₂
mcqs.explain: Both sides show 2 Na, 4 H and 2 O atoms, so every element balances.

mcqs.q: A student tries to balance H₂ + O₂ → H₂O by rewriting the product as H₂O₂. Why is this not acceptable?
options: It is allowed as long as the same subscript change is made on the other side.
The atoms now balance, but the equation shows too many molecules.
H₂O₂ is a different substance, so the equation no longer shows this reaction.
Hydrogen and oxygen cannot form a compound with two oxygen atoms.
mcqs.explain: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide. Changing a subscript changes the chemical, so balancing must be done with multipliers in front instead.

mcqs.q: How many atoms in total are shown by 2Ca(OH)₂?
mcqs.explain: Each Ca(OH)₂ has 1 Ca, 2 O and 2 H, which is 5 atoms; the multiplier 2 doubles all of them.

mcqs.q: In the equation 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, what does the 2 written in front of MgO tell you?
options: Two extra oxygen atoms are joined to each magnesium oxide.
Twice as much magnesium oxide forms, by mass, as magnesium.
Two units of magnesium oxide: two Mg atoms and two O atoms.
The magnesium is doubled, but the oxygen in it is not.
mcqs.explain: A multiplier in normal script multiplies every atom in the formula that follows it.

mcqs.q: What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃? (Ar: Ca 40, C 12, O 16)
mcqs.explain: 40 + 12 + (3 x 16) = 100, using each relative atomic mass in the number shown in the formula.

mcqs.q: What is the relative formula mass of magnesium nitrate, Mg(NO₃)₂? (Ar: Mg 24, N 14, O 16)
mcqs.explain: The subscript 2 multiplies the whole NO₃ group: 24 + 2 x (14 + 48) = 148.

mcqs.q: 50 g of calcium carbonate is heated in an open tube until it fully decomposes: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. The calcium oxide left has a mass of 28 g. What mass of carbon dioxide escaped?
options: 0 g
mcqs.explain: The masses of the products must total the 50 g of reactant, so the gas accounts for 50 - 28 = 22 g.

mcqs.q: In a balanced equation, why does the sum of the relative formula masses of the reactants equal that of the products?
options: Every reaction is done in a sealed container, so nothing at all can escape.
The same atoms are present on both sides, just rearranged, so the totals match.
The balancing numbers are chosen to make the two mass totals come out equal.
Each formula on the left has the same relative formula mass as one on the right.
mcqs.explain: Equal atom counts of every element mean the same relative atomic masses are being added up on each side.

mcqs.q: Calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, has a relative formula mass of 100. What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in it? (Ar: Ca 40, C 12, O 16)
mcqs.explain: Three oxygen atoms contribute 3 x 16 = 48 out of the relative formula mass of 100.

mcqs.q: Ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃, has a relative formula mass of 80. What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in it? (Ar: N 14, H 1, O 16)
mcqs.explain: The formula shows two nitrogen atoms, so (2 x 14) / 80 x 100 = 35.0%.

mcqs.q: Sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, has a relative formula mass of 98. Which expression gives the percentage by mass of hydrogen in it? (Ar: H 1)
mcqs.explain: The formula shows two hydrogen atoms, each of relative atomic mass 1, out of a relative formula mass of 98.

mcqs.q: Magnesium ribbon is heated in an open crucible until it has fully reacted. What happens to the mass of the solid, and why?
options: It rises, because oxygen from the air has combined with the magnesium.
It falls, because the magnesium burns away and is lost into the air.
It rises, because heating expands the metal and larger pieces weigh more.
It stays the same, since no atoms can be gained or lost from the crucible.
mcqs.explain: When a metal reacts with oxygen the mass of the oxide produced is greater than the mass of the metal.

mcqs.q: Copper carbonate is heated in an open test tube: CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂. The mass of solid in the tube falls. Why?
options: Heat from the flame has destroyed some of the carbon and oxygen atoms.
The solid evaporates, so copper carbonate is lost from the tube as vapour.
The copper oxide formed is less dense than the copper carbonate was.
Carbon dioxide gas is produced and escapes, taking its mass away.
mcqs.explain: The carbon dioxide leaves the tube, so the copper oxide is the only solid product left to be weighed.

mcqs.q: In an open flask on a balance, calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. The reading falls. Which statement is correct?
options: Mass is not conserved here, because the flask was not sealed with a bung.
The carbon dioxide produced has no mass of its own, so the products weigh less.
Some of the acid particles have been destroyed in making the new products.
Mass is conserved; the carbon dioxide has left and is no longer weighed.
mcqs.explain: The equation shows a gaseous product. In a non-enclosed system it escapes, so the balance no longer holds all the products.

mcqs.q: The same reaction is repeated in a flask sealed with a bung, standing on a balance. What happens to the reading?
options: It stays the same, because the carbon dioxide is still inside the flask.
It falls, because once the carbon is a gas its particles have no mass.
It rises, because the gas particles press outwards on the sealed flask.
It falls a little, because gas can pass out through the glass walls.
mcqs.explain: No particles enter or leave, so every atom that was weighed at the start is still being weighed at the end.

mcqs.q: 0.24 g of magnesium ribbon is burned in an open crucible and 0.40 g of white solid is left. Which statement explains the increase in terms of the particle model?
options: The magnesium particles have grown larger as they took in heat energy.
Oxygen molecules from the air have bonded to magnesium in the solid.
Extra particles were created in the crucible as the bright flame burned.
Air became trapped between the particles of the white powder as it formed.
mcqs.explain: Particles have crossed into the crucible from the air, so the solid now contains 0.16 g of oxygen as well as the metal.

mcqs.q: A student measures the same volume of solution five times and gets five slightly different readings. What does this show?
options: The student was careless; accurate work gives the same value each time.
Whenever a measurement is made there is some uncertainty in the result.
A mistake has been made, so all five of the readings must be wrong.
The volume of the solution changed a little between the readings.
mcqs.explain: Uncertainty is a property of measurement itself, so repeated readings are not expected to agree exactly.

mcqs.q: A student records five titres: 24.10, 24.15, 24.20, 25.90 and 24.15 cm³. What should be done before estimating the uncertainty?
options: Include all five of the titres in the mean, since every reading must be used.
Use 25.90 as the measure of spread, as it is the largest value found.
Repeat the titration once more and report only that final reading.
Set the results out to show their distribution and treat 25.90 as anomalous.
mcqs.explain: Displaying the distribution makes the value lying outside it obvious, and it is excluded before the mean and range are found.

mcqs.q: Four titres are recorded: 24.10, 24.15, 24.20 and 24.15 cm³. What is the range of these measurements?
options: 0.05 cm³
0.10 cm³
mcqs.explain: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values: 24.20 - 24.10 = 0.10 cm³.

mcqs.q: The mean of a set of titres is 24.15 cm³ and their range is 0.10 cm³. How should the result be quoted?
mcqs.explain: The range is used about the mean, so half of it is placed on each side of the mean value.
